10250102.text: The ominous aura of that monster has indeed begun to fade.

10250103.text: The effects of the Sigil of Permission last but a short time.

10250104.text: It will be some time before the Overlord of the Vortex can make any waves again.

10250105.text: We are indebted to you for your assistance. If the adepti hadn't happened to be here, the future of Liyue Harbor would surely have been in great jeopardy...

10250106.text: Hmph, save your flattery. We didn't just "happen" to be here... Surely you won't pretend to have forgotten the reason for which we came?

10250107.text: Come now, there's no need for such harsh words, Cloud Retainer.

10250108.text: I've heard that when Ningguang began learning to do business, she had already started setting aside part of her then-limited income in preparation for building the Jade Chamber.

10250109.text: At first, it was only the size of a small room. But with continued expansion, it has become the palace that lies before you now.

10250110.text: It is a testament to Ningguang's entire life, both as a businesswoman and as the backbone of the Liyue Qixing.

10250111.text: Seeing the Jade Chamber destroyed in the defense of Liyue means much to her. To me, such cooperation and sacrifice deserves at least some recognition, don't you agree?

10250112.text: Well, I was really hoping you would say that such sacrifice could at least be used as some leverage in our negotiations.

10250114.text: Thank you all for hearing me out. We know very well why the adepti came here today... But please forgive us, we cannot yield to your wishes.

10250116.text: 3,700 years... According to our records, the adepti signed a contract with Rex Lapis to protect Liyue 3,700 years ago.

10250117.text: Even to this very day, Liyue and its lands have stood the test of time, immovable as stone, just as it was thousands of years before. This is truly no small feat.

10250118.text: But that does not mean that the Liyue of today is the same city as it was all those years ago.

10250119.text: Do not merely cast your protective gaze upon the land. Instead, focus your sights on our city and each of the citizens that dwell within it.

10250120.text: Are you questioning our means of protecting Liyue?

10250122.text: I mean no offense. I simply hope that our adepti forebearers would see Liyue in a new light.

10250123.text: Hah, "forebearers" you say. One doubts you would be fit to be part of such a lineage...

10250124.text: This morning, Rex Lapis appeared to me in a dream.

10250126.text: In the dream, I yearned to tell him that we Qixing, though mortal, are equally bound to the contract. Each passing generation of the Qixing leaves many things of value to be inherited by the next generation.

10250127.text: I also thought to tell him how the past generations of Qixing had strove under his rule to survive in our mortal world, establishing a network of contracts which has since come to be known as "trade."

10250128.text: But I dared not speak. I could only gaze at him in silence until the moment I awoke.

10250130.text: We're all on the same side here...

10250131.text: Yet another perspective... What are you trying to say, Outlander?

10250132.text: When there is discord between the guardians and those they were meant to defend...

10250133.text: Harmony becomes very difficult to restore.

10250134.text: Right, that's something that happened in Mondstadt — it's a story about the Four Winds and the people of the Anemo Archon.

10250135.text: The Anemo Archon sought to quell the strife between the two sides, because he believed that such conflict would only scar the hearts of both and that nothing good would come of it...

10250136.text: This is what we learned in the City of Freedom.

10250137.text: Each of the Seven Nations has its own scars from the past.

10250138.text: Though your point is the very height of simplicity...

10250139.text: As adepti, we've become a laughingstock, to be chastised thus by an outlander who has lent us such succor.

10250140.text: Alright, alright. Didn't Ningguang suggest that we should focus on the city and each of its citizens? I know I already have, so why not see for yourselves?

10250141.text: I apologize for appearing in full armor. I'm afraid I cannot show the proper courtesies.

10250143.text: I am Fengyan, a sergeant of the Millelith. I have come to extend my thanks to the adepti.

10250144.text: I thought this battle would perhaps be my last. But thanks to the aid of the adepti, our forces were not as badly battered as I feared we might be.

10250145.text: Although I am a mere mortal soldier, I promise to hold the line and never betray the grace given to us by the illuminated adepti this day.

10250148.text: Huh? Why does everyone look so down? Didn't we just beat that big monster?

10250149.text: Hahaha! Weren't you frightened, dear? It was quite the predicament...

10250150.text: I wasn't afraid. All the strong Millelith guards were there, and those powerful heroes with their Visions were there... Everyone was there!

10250151.text: When danger is near, everyone always protects me. And the rest of the time, they make fun toys, and tasty snacks, and... and loads of things that make the harbor so pretty!

10250152.text: Thanks for protecting Liyue Harbor! Please come visit us for the next Lantern Rite!

10250153.text: Unfortunately, we wouldn't be able to participate.

10250156.text: Oh, okay... It must be hard being an adeptus.

10250158.text: You see, this is what Liyue is like today.

10250159.text: The country of contracts is grateful to the adepti for their protection. But it is no longer necessary for the city to rely on the adepti's power to solve every little niggling matter.

10250160.text: Although their blood is weak, there is still strength to be found in those we call mortals...

10250161.text: The time of contracts between gods and Liyue has long since passed. Now is the time of contracts between Liyue and its people.

10250162.text: Hmm, seeing the port around us now, it is hard not to feel a bit out of place... wouldn't you say so, Cloud Retainer?

10250163.text: Your line of inquiry is askew. One did not spearhead this expedition to Liyue Harbor...

10250164.text: Hmm... seems like the adepti have had a change of heart.

10250170.text: Yes, one understands what the Conqueror of Demons means. The city of Liyue has changed much after our long separation.

10250171.text: One fears that by the time one finally grasps the new contracts of Liyue, you humans would have once again changed the place beyond recognition.

10250172.text: Fair enough. Away we shall, and return whence we came...

10250174.text: Since we adepti have consensus, then one shall persist no further.

10250175.text: But how will we ensure that the Liyue Qixing will not simply exploit their power once we depart? In my view, that is still a thing to be guarded against...

10250177.text: Alright, Moon Carver. You needn't worry. It seems to me that this right of supervision is best left to the people of Liyue.

10250178.text: Whew... Looks like the conflict between humans and adepti was avoided. All's well that ends well, huh?

10251501.text: Is there anything I can do for you two? I'm afraid that Wangsheng Funeral Parlor isn't in the best state to receive guests.

10251502.text: We've come to see Zhongli. Could you please tell him we're here?

10251503.text: Unfortunately, Zhongli isn't here at the moment. It seems he went to Northland Bank.

10251504.text: Doesn't the Northland Bank belong to the Fatui?

10251505.text: Last time we saw Zhongli was before we went to the Golden House...

10251506.text: Do you think he doesn't know about the attack on Liyue? Visiting the Fatui at a time like this could only mean more trouble!

10251507.text: We had better go and make sure that everything is okay.

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for Zhongli at Northland Bank

10252101.text: The clean-up of the premises, managing the crowds as they exit, making an account of the Rite... There's much that remains to be done. I didn't miss anything, did I?

10250201.text: You call this "cooperation between Harbingers"? Cooperation involves communication, you know...

10250202.text: Hehe, don't take it to heart, Childe. Besides, aren't you happy that you got to skip the formalities and bring chaos to the land? I'm sure you must've enjoyed that...

10250203.text: ...Oh, it seems that some of your friends have arrived.

10250204.text: Hey, it's Zhongli and Childe! And... you! You're also one of the Harbingers...

10250206.text: Haha, it's you two. I believe we've met once before... In the City of Bards, was it? I'm glad you still remember my name.

10250207.text: Ah, right. I imagine that it must have been rather hard to forget watching helplessly as something precious was snatched away from your friend.

10250213.text: #Well, if it isn't {NICKNAME}. This is our first time seeing each other since Liyue was nearly wiped off the map. This is certainly a bit... awkward, wouldn't you say?

10250214.text: Hmph, Paimon knew that we should never have trusted a Fatui Harbinger!

10250215.text: Aw, now don't say that. Sure, I may have misled you, but I never had anything against you personally...

10250216.text: Besides, I thought we were getting along quite well together, didn't you? Except for that little tussle we had at the end... Haha.

10250217.text: Nothing personal, we just have... different views, that's all. Of course, you may very well hold this against me, but that's up to you...

10250218.text: The real deceivers here are Signora and Zhongli... curse them for leading me on.

10250210.text: #No, don't let her get to you, {NICKNAME}...

10250211.text: You've yet to gather the powers of all seven elements, and our last battle at the Golden House was almost more than you could handle...

10250212.text: So it might be best to keep things peaceful this time, seeing that two of the Harbingers are here.

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow the road up to Yujing Terrace

10250301.text: ...Well, since we're going through with this Rite of Parting... I guess it means that those rumors hit the nail on the head.

10250302.text: So Rex Lapis is really... But they didn't catch the culprit, did they?

10250303.text: Ah, come on, do you think that the assassin could have been a normal person? You know what I think? I don't think any of the gossip on the streets you hear from those shady types is worth anything.

10250304.text: There's only one real possibility in my mind. I've heard that the assassin was that Fatui fellow. Youngish, pretty high in rank — I think they called him Childe.

10250305.text: The Fatui? They certainly are very suspicious. Who knows what those greedy, crooked folks...

10250306.text: Shh! Lower your voice! If the Fatui catch you in their sights, Rex Lapis won't be around to protect you this time!

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow the road up to Yujing Terrace

10250401.text: You know that god from the ocean couldn't have just shown up out of nowhere. I mean, it's been two thousand years since Rex Lapis subdued it.

10250402.text: Yes, and to think that this happened right on the heels of the incident with Rex Lapis, too...

10250403.text: Say, do you think the person who assassinated our Lord and released that evil god might have been one and the same?

10250404.text: Now that you mention it, that's very possible. Yes... it's very possible indeed.

10250405.text: I mean, it all fits together! That person must have colluded with the evil god to harm Rex Lapis. Ugh, that wicked, black-hearted scoundrel...

10250406.text: Still, what sort of supernatural prowess must this person possess to be able to do such things? I have never heard of such a person in all my years.

10250407.text: Ah, forget it. Guessing's no use to us. Look, the Millelith over there looks like he's about to make an announcement. Let's hear what the Ministry of Civil Affairs has to say first.

10250501.text: Hear ye all the Qixing's words:

10250502.text: Though a dragon soars ageless as the mountains, it too must return to dust. This is common knowledge.

10250503.text: Gods and adepti live glorious lives, but both light and shadow have their season. So, too, must they face divinely-appointed trials.

10250504.text: Rumors and hearsay abound on the streets that Rex Lapis was murdered. Now, let the truth be revealed.

10250505.text: Having been thwarted in his trial, Rex Lapis' soul has recouped the celestial heights. He beseeches the people of Liyue to grieve not, and to let not their hearts be saddened.

10250506.text: Nor are they to believe street-borne rumors or indulge in baseless speculation.

10250507.text: #Ah... Um, Paimon needs a translation on what the Qixing's announcement said, {NICKNAME}.

10250511.text: Something feels off. Why would they suddenly give up looking for the murderer? Not to mention how this excuse sounds like something they just made up on the spot.

10250512.text: Could the Qixing already have known that Rex Lapis wasn't dead? But Zhongli said that neither they nor the adepti knew anything...

10250513.text: Hmm... Did Zhongli tell them in secret after his Gnosis changed hands?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the site of the Rite of Parting

10250601.text: Look, it's Ningguang and Keqing. Are they saying something? Are their speeches over?

10250602.text: ...As said previously, Rex Lapis' soul returning to the heavens is the end of the contract, and it is also the end of an era.

10250603.text: 3,700 years of contracts, burnt and reduced to ash...

10250604.text: We, the people of Liyue were indeed prosperous. But blinded by our prosperity, we forgot that time can be pitiless.

10250605.text: The long, unending dream of our archon walking among us...

10250607.text: Now that we have awoken from our dream, we must learn to say farewell.

10250608.text: Will you stand with us as we reestablish our contracts — as we build a new age of prosperity?

10250609.text: So concludes the words of her Eminence, the Tianquan.

10250610.text: Does Her Eminence the Yuheng have anything to add?

10250611.text: Eh? Is she looking this way?

10250613.text: Yikes! She really is looking our way!

10250614.text: Is that the traveler who they say defeated the ancient god?

10250616.text: The Liyue Qixing always repay their debts. And as you have heard, our eyes see far and our reach is long.

10250617.text: Name your price. You deserve that much.

10250620.text: Well... could you help me put up some missing person posters...?

10250701.text: As for the mortals and adepti of Liyue... what shape shall our relationship take from now on?

10250801.text: Ha, and to think I'd put my best perfume on before coming here, thinking you'd like it...

10250802.text: But it seems as if those perfumes really were meant to be offered to Rex Lapis.

10250803.text: Well, that's fine. Suffer no rivals in love, they say, and that's three gone in one stroke. *chuckles*

10250902.text: Hmm. Now that I think about it, if everyone's of the same mind as me...

10250903.text: Perhaps mementos for Rex Lapis might be the best short-term business opportunity...

10251801.text: Roping you in was possibly the most masterful move we could have made. I believe that future generations will say so too, when our deeds come up for their review.

10251901.text: Heh. Why, you... Were you just trying to look cool earlier, or are you really that selfless?

10251902.text: If you were looking for someone, you could have just told me that in private...

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the people taking part in the rite
Look for Zhongli at the scene

10251002.text: Look at this. Everyone in Liyue's caught up in their emotions, thinking that they'll never see Rex Lapis again...

10251003.text: ...And here you are, looking all relaxed!

10251004.text: Hahaha. Why would I not feel more at ease after laying down the burden I have borne for 3,700 years?

10251005.text: Right, if the two of you can spare the time, I should treat you to a meal at the Xinyue Kiosk.

10251006.text: Hah! That sounds like big talk, Zhongli. Paimon might have believed you if you were treating us to some Third-Round Knockout, but you'd have to pay out your nose just to stand inside Xinyue Kiosk. Are you sure you can afford it?

10251008.text: You're right, I do lack the Mora.

10251010.text: But why would Morax lack Mora?

10251012.text: As the Rex Lapis Morax, I can easily create Mora. But since I have chosen to walk this earth as the mortal Zhongli, I should abide by the same rules that mortals do.

10251013.text: When I was journeying with you, though I still had the Gnosis in hand, I knew that I must soon retire from my role as an archon. So I had to... rehearse a little, for my new life.

10251014.text: Oh, no wonder! Paimon gets it now. You didn't look at the price tags when we were spending because you've never had to.

10251015.text: But since you weren't used to not being able to just make more Mora as and when you wanted to, you had to try becoming a parasite to society who lives off of other peoples' credit...

10251016.text: Well, we were only spending Fatui money. You don't have to say it like that...

10251017.text: In the city of commerce, we do not merely exchange money or goods. We also exchange knowledge, memories, and foresight, as well as positions, roles, and lives.

10251018.text: The archon Morax could never experience life as the true mortal Zhongli could, no matter how many times he descended to be with his people.

10251019.text: #Haha, I must thank you for that, {NICKNAME}.

10251020.text: I will treasure the memories that I made as Zhongli, traveling the streets of Liyue with you.

10251022.text: That is true, but there is no journey that does not end. No meetings without partings.

10251023.text: Mm... Paimon thinks that we should make a move and continue our search for The Seven.

10251024.text: I fear that continuing your journey may be difficult. The nation that neighbors Liyue by sea, Inazuma, is presently closed.

10252501.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

10252601.text: (The seven kites used in the ceremony, which represent The Seven.)

10252602.text: #(How long before I find the one who took my {F#brother}{M#sister}?)

10252701.text: (Everlasting Incense... The lengths we went to to get our hands on that. The powders made from Glaze Lilies still remain at the bottom.)

10252702.text: (Two million, nine-hundred-and-ninety thousand Mora's worth of incense, going up in smoke... Ugh...)

10252801.text: (A specially prepared perfume, made from a exotic type of Silk Flower. It has a faint scent.)

10252802.text: (Still, why would Rex Lapis go for the scent preferred by older women...)

10252901.text: (As per the traditions of the Rite of Parting, the cleansing sound of the bell sees the soul of the immortal on its way.)

10252902.text: (It's hard to believe someone would store such a precious object in a teapot filled with cobwebs.)

10253001.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

10253101.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

10253201.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

10253301.text: Oh? Why are you hanging back here? Don't you want to get closer to the action?

10253302.text: You went through a lot to organize this rite, and this is a rare opportunity to see your journey bear fruit with your own eyes. You should make the most of it.

10253401.text: Paimon... can't... absorb so much information at once...

10253402.text: So, Zhongli, what sort of contract did you sign with the Cryo Archon? Paimon's so curious!

10253403.text: ...One of the clauses of our contract was not to divulge any of its contents.

10254001.text: Come to think of it, I wonder what business Mr. Zhongli has at the Northland Bank? He didn't tell me, either...
